kurz: How the tax office taxes rental income, when it refunds tax and how the BGB (Civil Code) limits the rental return.

bloecke.md:
For tax purposes, rental income belongs to income from letting and leasing (Einkünfte aus Vermietung und Verpachtung) under Section 21 EStG (Income Tax Act) and not to capital income. There is therefore no 25% flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer), no saver's allowance (Sparer-Pauschbetrag) and no withholding at source by a bank. The result is declared in the rental income annex (Anlage V), added to all other income and taxed at the personal marginal tax rate. In 2026, this is 42% from €69,879 and 45% from €277,826 of taxable income (Section 32a EStG).

The result is determined by a surplus calculation, that is, income minus income-related expenses (Werbungskosten). The cash-basis principle (Zufluss- und Abflussprinzip) of Section 11 EStG applies. What counts is the day of payment, not the period for which payment is made. Income includes the basic rent and advance payments for operating costs. The advance payments are immediately offset again as an expense and are therefore a pass-through item with a time lag.

bloecke.titel: Tax calculation for a let flat in the first year
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation with acquisition costs of €330,000 including incidental costs, a building share of 70%, construction year 1998 and a loan of €220,000 at 3.97%.

bloecke.md:
## Tax loss and cash result

The loss of €4,580 arises only in the tax calculation. Two items have a different effect there than on the bank account. The building's tax depreciation (AfA) of €4,620 reduces the result without any money flowing out for it. Repayment costs money but is not an income-related expense, because it reallocates wealth and does not create an expense. Anyone who confuses the two takes the flat for a tax-saving scheme, although it requires top-up payments every month.

The annuity is 5.97% on €220,000, that is, 3.97% interest plus 2% initial repayment. That comes to €13,134 a year, of which around €8,700 is interest and €4,400 repayment.

- Rental income +€9,800
- Annuity −€13,134
- Management and maintenance −€1,060
- Cash result −€4,394

At a 42% marginal tax rate, the tax effect of the loss is around €1,920. Overall, this leaves top-up payments of about €2,470 a year, just over €205 a month, while the outstanding debt falls by €4,400. The owner therefore does not save any tax. They build up wealth in the property and pay for it with ongoing top-up payments and with risk.

## AfA on the building

The allowance for wear and tear (Absetzung für Abnutzung, AfA) is the only item of income-related expenses that costs no money. It exists only for letting; for owner-occupation, almost nothing is tax-deductible. Only the building is depreciated, never the land, because land does not wear out. The incidental purchase costs form part of the depreciable basis pro rata, to the extent that they are attributable to the building.

bloecke.formel: Depreciable basis = (Purchase price + Incidental purchase costs) × Building share
bloecke.erklaerung: The building share is derived from the ratio of the land value to the total value. It is not freely negotiable, but it is based on an estimate and is therefore a point of dispute.
variablen: real estate transfer tax (Grunderwerbsteuer), notary, land register, estate agent; like the purchase price, they are split between building and land
in cities often 60% to 75%, considerably less in expensive locations
bloecke.beispiel: €330,000 × 70% = €231,000 depreciable basis; at 2%, that is €4,620 of AfA a year.

bloecke.titel: Straight-line and declining-balance AfA on a building value of €300,000 over ten years
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation under Section 7(4) and (5a) EStG. With the declining-balance method, €120,379 has been depreciated after ten years instead of €90,000. Depreciation is thus brought forward; the total depreciation volume remains the same.

bloecke.md:
With acquisition costs of €330,000 and 2% AfA, each percentage point of building share yields €66 of depreciation a year, that is, a depreciable volume of €3,300 over 50 years. A difference of ten percentage points therefore corresponds to €33,000 that can or cannot be depreciated.

By default, the tax office uses the calculation aid (Arbeitshilfe) of the Federal Ministry of Finance, which shows very high land shares in expensive locations. The Federal Fiscal Court (BFH) has ruled that this calculation aid is not binding on the courts. A different allocation must be plausible and documented in the purchase contract or supported by an expert report. A clearly unrealistic contractual clause is rejected.

## Timing of the deduction of income-related expenses

Loan interest, the property manager's fee, running costs that cannot be passed on to tenants, insurance, account charges, journeys to the property, tax adviser fees for the rental income annex and maintenance expenditure (Erhaltungsaufwand) are deductible immediately. Maintenance expenditure includes everything that keeps existing items in good repair or replaces them in an up-to-date form, for example new windows, a new heating system or new flooring. Construction costs (Herstellungskosten), by contrast, are enlargements and substantial improvements, for example an extension, the conversion of the attic or a bathroom installed for the first time. They are included in the AfA and take effect over decades.

If a buyer spends more than 15% of the building's acquisition costs on repairs and modernisation in the first three years after the purchase (net, excluding VAT), the entire amount is reclassified as **post-acquisition renovation costs (anschaffungsnahe Herstellungskosten)**.

With a building share of €231,000, the limit is €34,650. At €36,000 net, the immediate deduction is lost entirely. Instead of €36,000 in the year of payment, 2% of it is then deductible each year, that is, €720. At a 42% marginal tax rate, this results in a tax effect of €302 a year instead of €15,120 all at once. Enlargements and expenses that usually arise every year are excluded. Anyone close to the limit should postpone work to the fourth year.

bloecke.titel: Spreading under Section 82b EStDV (Income Tax Implementing Ordinance)
bloecke.md: Larger maintenance expenditure on residential buildings may be spread evenly over two to five years. This pays off if the immediate deduction falls in a year with low income or creates a loss that the other income can no longer offset. The tax effect always depends on the marginal tax rate of the year in question. For example, €30,000 of expenditure in a year with a 28% marginal tax rate saves less tax than five times €6,000 in years at 42%.

## Loss offsetting and its limits

The most important difference from a portfolio lies in loss offsetting. Under Section 20(6) EStG, losses from capital assets may only be offset against income from capital assets, separately in their own loss offset pots. This restriction does not apply to losses from letting and leasing. They reduce total taxable income and are therefore also offset against employment income. Anything that cannot be offset in one year can be carried back to the two preceding years or carried forward indefinitely under Section 10d EStG.

There are two restrictions. The first concerns letting at a reduced rent under Section 21(2) EStG. If the rent is below 66% of the local market rent, the deduction of income-related expenses is reduced proportionately. Between 50% and 66%, a forecast of the total surplus (Totalüberschussprognose) decides; below 50%, the expenses are always split. Landlords who let cheaply to relatives should know the threshold and document the local rent.

The second restriction is the intention to generate income (Einkünfteerzielungsabsicht). For long-term letting of residential property, the tax authorities assume that it exists, so that even losses over many years are recognised. For holiday flats with considerable personal use or for fixed-term contracts, the tax office requires a forecast of the total surplus. If it turns out negative, the letting is treated as a hobby (Liebhaberei), and the losses are disregarded for tax purposes.

## Ten-year period on sale

Under Section 23 EStG, the sale is tax-free if more than ten years lie between acquisition and disposal. The period is counted from the dates of the notarised purchase contracts, not from handover or entry in the land register. If the sale contract is signed two weeks too early, the entire gain is taxable at the personal tax rate. An exemption threshold (Freigrenze) applies to all private disposal transactions (private Veräußerungsgeschäfte) in a year. The total gain remains tax-free only if it is less than €1,000. From €1,000, the entire amount is taxable and not just the part above the threshold.

bloecke.titel: Tax exemption of the capital gain (Section 23 EStG)
bloecke.unter: Use for your own residential purposes in the year of sale and in the two preceding years replaces the holding period, but only without interruption.

felder.text: Owner-occupied continuously since acquisition, or in the year of sale and the two preceding calendar years. Letting only after moving out in the year of sale does no harm.
Period expired, use irrelevant. The usual case for a home that is sold.
The gain counts towards taxable income, and the personal marginal tax rate applies. The AfA claimed increases the gain further.
After ten years, neither the AfA nor the letting plays a role. This is the plannable exit for a buy-to-let investment.

bloecke.md:
The purchase contract is concluded in January 2019 for €300,000; the building share is €210,000. From 2019 to 2025, 2% AfA is claimed for seven years, a total of €29,400. The property is sold in January 2026 for €380,000; notary and estate agent cost €5,000.

Taxable gain = 380,000 − (300,000 − 29,400) − 5,000 = €104,400

Under Section 23(3) sentence 4 EStG, the AfA claimed is deducted from the acquisition costs. The gain therefore increases by the amount with which tax was saved earlier. At a 42% marginal tax rate, this sale costs around €43,800 in income tax. Three more years of waiting would have been needed for the tax exemption.

If more than three properties are bought and sold again within five years, the owner is regarded under established case law as a commercial property dealer (gewerblicher Grundstückshändler). The ten-year period then no longer applies, trade tax (Gewerbesteuer) and record-keeping obligations arise, and the properties become current assets without AfA. The three-property limit (Drei-Objekt-Grenze) is an indicative rule and not an exemption threshold. If the activity is clearly systematic, the sale of fewer properties can also be commercial.

## Switching between owner-occupation and letting

If an owner-occupied flat is let, the deduction of income-related expenses begins with the demonstrable intention to let. Preparatory renovation costs then already count as well. The AfA continues to be based on the historical acquisition costs and not on today's market value. The AfA volume for the years of owner-occupation is lost. After ten years of owner-occupation, depreciation is therefore only applied over the remaining useful life.

Conversely, every deduction ends when the owner moves in, that is, for interest, AfA and maintenance. The switch also has consequences under Section 23 EStG. If the flat is let for another two years before the ten years have expired and is then sold, the exemption for owner-occupation that the seller wanted to rely on no longer applies.

## Tenancy law as a ceiling on returns

Besides the market, the BGB also limits the return on a flat. With sitting tenants, the rent rises considerably more slowly than inflation would suggest.

bloecke.titel: Modernisation under tenancy law and tax law
bloecke.md:
A flat of 80 square metres is let at a basic rent of €6.50 per square metre. It is modernised for €60,000, of which €15,000 is a maintenance portion that must be deducted.

- Recoverable: €45,000 × 8% = €3,600 a year, that is, €300 a month.
- That would be €3.75 per square metre, so the cap applies. Because the initial rent is below €7, at most €2 per square metre within six years is permitted, that is, €160 a month.

For tax purposes, a modernisation within the meaning of tenancy law is not automatically construction expenditure. If existing components such as windows or heating are renewed in an up-to-date form, the €45,000 is usually also immediately deductible maintenance expenditure. The situation is different, for example, with an extension or a substantial improvement of the building. The €45,000 then counts as construction costs and at 2% yields only €900 of AfA a year, while the €15,000 maintenance portion is immediately deductible. In this case, an allocation that relieves the tenant helps the landlord with tax, and vice versa.

The tax depends on the difference between rent and income-related expenses. In the example, [[Tax depreciation (AfA)|AfA]] is the largest item of income-related expenses after interest and costs no money. Repayment is the largest payment item after interest and is not deductible. A tax loss is therefore possible with a positive cash flow, and equally a taxable profit with an empty account.

Under Section 573 BGB, ordinary termination requires a legitimate interest. Recognised grounds are above all personal need (Eigenbedarf) of the landlord, of family members or of members of the household (Section 573(2) no. 2 BGB), a culpable, not insignificant breach of contractual obligations by the tenant (no. 1) and termination for economic exploitation (Verwertungskündigung) if the tenancy prevents the owner from making appropriate economic use of the property and the owner would suffer considerable disadvantages as a result (no. 3). Expressly excluded are the prospect of a higher rent on re-letting and a sale in connection with conversion into flat ownership (Wohnungseigentum).

The notice periods depend on the length of the tenancy. They are three months, six months after five years and nine months after eight years (Section 573c BGB). The tenant can object to the termination under the hardship clause (Sozialklausel) of Section 574 BGB.

On a purchase, Section 566 BGB applies (“sale does not break a lease”). The buyer takes over the existing contract, with all agreements and the previous rent level. If a let flat has been converted into flat ownership, Section 577a BGB blocks termination for personal need and for economic exploitation for three years. The federal states may extend this period to up to ten years in tight markets. In addition, the tenant has a right of first refusal under Section 577 BGB on conversion. Buyers who want to move into a let flat themselves must therefore above all expect a waiting period.

mitnehmen: Rental income falls under Section 21 EStG and is taxed at the personal marginal tax rate instead of the flat-rate withholding tax; in return, unlike in a portfolio, losses can be offset against all other income.
AfA applies only to the building share, so the allocation of the purchase price and incidental costs between land and building is the most consequential figure in the purchase contract.
If net repair costs in the first three years exceed 15% of the building's acquisition costs, the immediate deduction is lost for the entire amount.
On a sale within ten years, the AfA claimed increases the taxable gain, so that the earlier tax advantage is subsequently taxed again.
The rent brake (Mietpreisbremse), the rent increase cap (Kappungsgrenze) and the cap on the modernisation rent increase limit the return regardless of what the market would bear.

Repair and modernisation expenditure within three years of the purchase that exceeds 15% of the building's acquisition costs, net (Section 6(1) no. 1a EStG). It is not immediately deductible and only has an effect through the AfA.

Increase in the annual rent by 8% of the recoverable modernisation costs (Section 559 BGB). It is capped at €3 per square metre in six years, or €2 for initial rents below €7.
